title: TRIP effect detection of medium manganese steel based on the MBN signal
abstract: In recent years, m-Mn (medium manganese) steel has gained increasing attention as a promising material for improving the crashworthiness and lightweight of vehicles, owing to its enhanced strength and ductility characteristics. However, the Transformation Induced Plasticity (TRIP) effect makes it challenging to accurately predict the microstructure and mechanical properties of m-Mn steel parts after forming. To overcome this issue, the Magnetic Barkhausen noise (MBN) detection technique is being employed to investigate the mechanism of TRIP effect on m-Mn steel, which could pave the way for the development of a non-destructive testing method for assessing the microstructure and mechanical properties of m-Mn steel parts. By analyzing the variation of MBN peak values of m-Mn steel and dual-phase steel DP1180 during the tensile process, it was found that the peak value of MBN signals increases continuously after the m-Mn steel is yielded due to the TRIP effect. Furthermore, a new strain-transformation model based on the O-C model was proposed to calculate the martensite content of m-Mn steel at all stages of elasticity and plasticity. By combining the detection data of MBN signals during the tensile process of m-Mn steel with the proposed strain-phase transformation model, a non-destructive testing method for the martensite content of m-Mn steel was established and compared with the traditional XRD test method. The results obtained from the testing of the martensite content of the corner of m-Mn steel U-shaped parts after stamping using the MBN testing method (6.56%, 9.94%) and the XRD testing method (7.42%, 9.26%) showed that the error between the two methods is less than 12%.
journal: Journal of Magnetism and Magnetic Materials
